rationale: A is better calibrated and more internally coherent: it explains why specialization, partner-led acquisition, land-and-expand, outcome-oriented pricing, and trust reinforce one another without relying on a conspicuously precise unsupported statistic. B is somewhat more operational through its sequencing, but its unsourced claim that partners can generate 40–60% of pipeline and its broad prescriptions about certifications and discounting lighthouse clients weaken its evidentiary discipline. A also states the core strategy more clearly and avoids implying that a single execution template fits every managed-services market.
